tempo.basis: from three complete recordings, median 2:20 (Kaufmann/Deutsch 2:16, Bostridge/Pappano 2:20, Oxford Lieder live, Stone Records, with Kynoch 2:55), 1.5 s allowed for silence; 26 bars and a pickup, mostly 12/8 with three bars of 6/8 = 147.5 quarter notes = 98.3 dotted quarters; Wolf marks it Sanfte Bewegung und immer sehr zart

phrases: Over treetops and fields of grain, into the radiance,
ˈyːbər ˈvɪpfəl ʊnt ˈzaːtən ɪn deːn ɡlants hɪˈnaɪn
who can guess them, who could catch them?
veːr maːk ziː ɛrˈraːtən veːr ˈhoːltə ziː aɪn
Thoughts rock to and fro, the night keeps silent,
ɡəˈdaŋkən zɪç ˈviːɡən diː naxt ɪst fɛrˈʃviːɡən
If only she alone would guess who has thought of her,
ɛrˈrɛːt ɛs nuːr ˈaɪnə veːr an ziː ɡəˈdaxt
in the rustling of the groves, when no one is awake any more
baɪm ˈraʊʃən deːr ˈhaɪnə vɛn ˈniːmant meːr vaxt
but the clouds that fly by,
my love is silent and lovely as the night.
maɪn liːp ɪst fɛrˈʃviːɡən ʊnt ʃøːn viː diː naxt

facts.key: two flats at the start; two sharps from bar 6, two flats from bar 13, two sharps from bar 15 to the end (closing in D major)
facts.time: 12/8, with single bars of 6/8 at bars 8, 17 and 23

notes: Words by Joseph von Eichendorff; Wolf's setting 1888 (Eichendorff-Lieder). IPA follows sung German (Bühnenaussprache): r rolled or flipped, final -er as [ər], ch after front vowels [ç], after a/o/u [x]. Literal translation, for meaning.
